questions.prompt: One dialog serves both create and edit. Explain how the app keeps the two modes apart and why an edit must not change the record's identity.

keyPoints.text: Create mints a new id and adds a record; edit keeps the existing id and replaces one record.
keyPoints.quote: **Create** mints a new id and adds a record.

keyPoints.text: The mode is made explicit by a single variable, editingExpenseId, which the submit handler checks.
keyPoints.quote: The app makes the mode explicit with one variable, `editingExpenseId`, which `handleEntrySubmit` checks at `app.js:205`.

keyPoints.text: For any dual-mode form, find the one place the mode is decided and every place it is reset.
keyPoints.quote: Wherever a form serves two modes, find the single place the mode is decided and every place it is reset.

keyPoints.text: The entry, including a brand-new id, is built before the handler knows which mode it is in.
keyPoints.quote: builds the entry, including a brand-new id, *before* it knows the mode

keyPoints.text: Spread order is the mechanism: later keys win, so id: existing.id must come after ...entry.
keyPoints.quote: Spread order is the whole mechanism: later keys win, so `id: existing.id` must come after `...entry`.

keyPoints.text: Dropping that line does not duplicate the row; it silently re-keys the record, which test 1 catches.
keyPoints.quote: What it does is silently re-key the record to `expense-<uuid>`.

questions.prompt: Walk through the write path: why does the app persist before it publishes, and how deep must the copy it writes be?

keyPoints.text: Publishing means assigning to state, because that is what render() reads.
keyPoints.quote: "Publish" means assigning to `state`, because that is what `render()` reads.

keyPoints.text: If the write throws, nothing visible has changed and the user can retry.
keyPoints.quote: If the write throws, nothing visible has changed and the user can retry.

keyPoints.text: The three unguarded writers mutate first and save second, the wrong way round.
keyPoints.quote: do it the other way round: mutate, then save

keyPoints.text: When their save throws, memory has changed but storage has not, and the skipped render shows a third version.
keyPoints.quote: `render()` is skipped because the exception escapes the listener, so the screen shows a third version.

keyPoints.text: The edit branch can use a shallow spread because map and the updated object are new, so nothing shared is mutated.
keyPoints.quote: `map` returns a new array and `updated` is a new object, so nothing shared is mutated.

keyPoints.text: The create branch needs a deep copy (structuredClone at line 224); test 3 already fails if a shallow spread is swapped in.
keyPoints.quote: The existing test 3 already fails if you swap in a shallow spread

keyPoints.text: No total is stored; every render recomputes the KPIs from state, so an edit changes only one record.
keyPoints.quote: So an edit only has to change one record, and every KPI, chart and budget bar follows.

questions.prompt: What does the amount field actually deliver to validateEntry, and why does money handling need care in this app?

keyPoints.text: The number input sanitizes its value before app.js sees it.
keyPoints.quote: sanitizes its value before `app.js` sees it

keyPoints.text: Tests dispatch submit directly, skipping the browser's interactive validation.
keyPoints.quote: The tests dispatch `submit` directly, which skips that interactive validation.

keyPoints.text: Unparseable input therefore reaches validateEntry as 0 and gets the 'greater than zero' message.
keyPoints.quote: unparseable input reaches `validateEntry` as `0` and gets the "greater than zero" message

keyPoints.text: validateEntry is the gate the code can actually rely on.
keyPoints.quote: `validateEntry` is the gate the code can rely on

keyPoints.text: The date check also round-trips through toISOString(), which rejects impossible dates like 2026-02-30.
keyPoints.quote: a date-shaped string (line 792) that also survives a round trip through `toISOString()` (lines 793-795), which rejects `2026-02-30`

keyPoints.text: The decimal check uses a tolerance because 8.2 * 100 is 819.9999999999999.
keyPoints.quote: The two-decimal check uses a tolerance because `8.2 * 100` is `819.9999999999999`

keyPoints.text: Integer cents would remove the whole class of float problems.
keyPoints.quote: Integer cents remove that whole class of problem
